about: Which chapters use the interview-walkthrough layout. Groups are content, not code: the build reads this file, then still checks each listed chapter's own numbered headings and falls back to the normal chapter layout when they do not match. Only listed walkthrough chapters are affected; chapter-layout groups record the decision. 30 October 2026: Phases 1, 2 and 3 plus the Offline Sync pilot.

groups.title: Foundations
groups.note: Design Framework teaches the interview method and its 12-section template, and Non-Functional Requirements is the NFR menu; neither walks through one design problem, so both keep the normal chapter layout.

groups.title: Cross-cutting practices
groups.note: Accessibility, Localization & Internationalization and Security & Privacy teach practices that apply to every design. They have few time hints and no follow-up questions, so an interview timeline would be mostly empty; they keep the normal chapter layout.

groups.title: Cross-cutting design problems
groups.note: A cross-cutting quality designed as one interview problem, with time hints, trade-off tables and follow-up questions: Performance and Versioning & Backward Compatibility.

groups.title: Infrastructure components
groups.note: Bounded libraries and data-delivery problems, for example image loading, caching, pagination, file download, search and notification routing.

groups.title: Full apps
groups.note: Complete product systems, for example offline sync, feeds, chat, payments and media.

groups.title: SDK and platform features
groups.note: Platform layers and SDKs, for example authentication, analytics, telemetry, flags and deep links.

requirements.question: What would you say?
requirements.prompt: The interviewer gives you a one-line product prompt. Before reading on, say what the system must do, which qualities it must keep, and what you will leave out.
covers: Functional requirements: the user actions that must work, including without a network.
Non-functional requirements: latency, consistency, battery and data use.
Out of scope: name it, so the interviewer can redirect you early.

clarifying.question: What would you ask?
clarifying.prompt: Which questions would change your design? Ask them before you draw anything.
covers: Who shares the data, and on how many devices.
Data size and volume per user.
How often conflicts or failures are expected.
How fresh background data must be.

api.question: What would you say?
api.prompt: Sketch the requests and responses between the app and the server. Which fields make a retried request safe?
covers: An idempotency key on every mutation.
Versions or cursors that detect conflicts and fetch only changes.
How the contract keeps working for older installed app versions.
